the relationship between the development of social communication and the development of motor skills.

motor competency and social communicative skills are significantly correlated in preschool children with ASD.
motor competency is a key factor in social communication and that the relationship between these two areas is more pronounced in ASD than in TD and ID.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we have shown that motor deficits in ASD are not just about motor skills but are also related to social communication skills and that this is true for both the manual dexterity and the aiming and catching skills.
children with ASD and ID have motor deficits that may be related to their social communication deficits.
motor skills in children with ASD are impaired in a way that is different from those with ID.
The main takeaway from our work is that
children with autism spectrum disorders and intellectual disabilities have deficits in their motor skills, which can be associated with their social communication skills.
children with ASD have deficits in motor skills that are not just related to gross motor or fine motor skills, but also to the ability to integrate social cues with motor skills.
motor skills are important for social communication and should be considered when assessing and treating children with ASD.
